title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of getting started with AWS – account setup, console, Free Tier, billing alarms, and support.

questions.question: What is the email address you use to create an AWS account called?
questions.explanation: The email you sign up with becomes the root account login. IAM users are created separately.

questions.question: You should use the root account for everyday tasks like launching EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: False. Create an IAM user with administrative permissions for daily work. The root account is for account/billing management only.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required to create an AWS account?
questions.explanation: You don’t need a domain name. The card and phone are for identity verification.

questions.question: How can you quickly find a specific AWS service in the Management Console?
options: Type the service name in the search bar at the top
questions.explanation: The search bar is the fastest way. You can also star frequently used services to pin them.

questions.question: You launched an EC2 instance in the Oregon (us-west-2) region. Later you switch to Ohio (us-east-2). Why can’t you see the instance?
options: You need to refresh the browser
EC2 resources are region-specific and do not appear in other regions
The instance takes 24 hours to appear in the new region
questions.explanation: EC2 instances are tied to the region they were launched in. Always check the region selector.

questions.question: Which of the following is a global service, not bound to any region?
questions.explanation: IAM is global; S3 buckets are global in namespace but data resides in a region.

questions.question: How many hours per month of t2.micro EC2 usage are included in the 12‑Month Free Tier?
questions.explanation: 750 hours/month – that’s roughly enough to run one instance continuously for 31 days.

questions.question: Which of the following is an Always Free service?
questions.explanation: Lambda’s free tier 1M requests/month never expires. EC2 and RDS free tiers are 12‑months only.

questions.question: Elastic IP addresses are free as long as they are attached to a running instance.
questions.explanation: True. If attached to a running instance, there’s no charge. If unattached, you pay a small hourly fee.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a billing alarm?
options: To automatically stop resources when the budget is reached
To send a notification when estimated charges exceed a threshold
To limit the maximum spending on the account
To track the number of API calls
questions.explanation: Billing alarms are alert mechanisms, not spending caps. They trigger when thresholds are crossed.

questions.question: AWS provides a _______ Budget type that alerts you when any cost is detected, ideal for Free Tier users.
questions.explanation: Zero spend budget sends an alert as soon as any cost accrues, helping catch unintended usage.

questions.question: Where can you find a visual breakdown of your AWS costs by service?
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer lets you analyse your spending with graphs and filters. It’s accessible from the Billing Dashboard.

questions.question: Which support plan is free and includes 24/7 account and billing support?
questions.explanation: The Basic plan is free and provides account/billing customer service plus access to documentation and forums.

questions.question: Which AWS support plan offers a Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
questions.explanation: Only the Enterprise plan provides a dedicated TAM.

questions.question: What is the AWS Personal Health Dashboard used for?
options: Viewing health information of your own AWS resources
questions.explanation: Personal Health Dashboard shows events specific to your account and resources, unlike the public Service Health Dashboard.

questions.question: Trusted Advisor offers 7 core checks for free on Basic and Developer plans. Which area might it alert you about?
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor’s free checks include cost optimization (like unused IPs), security, and performance.

questions.question: The AWS Free Tier 12‑month clock begins when you launch your first EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: False. The 12‑month period starts the day you create your AWS account, not when you first use a service.

questions.question: Which service can you use to pin frequently accessed services in the AWS Console?
options: The star icon next to the service name
questions.explanation: Click the star to pin services; they’ll appear in the top navigation for quick access.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of creating an IAM user for yourself instead of using the root account?
options: IAM users are free; root account costs money
You can apply least‑privilege permissions and add MFA, reducing risk
IAM users can spend more money
questions.explanation: IAM users let you follow the security best practice of granting only necessary permissions, and avoid exposing root credentials.

questions.question: Where can you find the custom sign‑in URL for IAM users in your account?
questions.explanation: The IAM Dashboard shows a 'Sign-in URL for IAM users' which you can customise with an alias.

questions.question: You run two t2.micro EC2 instances continuously for a full month (30 days). Will you exceed the Free Tier limit?
options: No, because t2.micro is always free
Yes, because 750 hours/month is total across all instances, and 2 × 720h = 1440h
No, because the Free Tier resets daily
Yes, but only if you use Windows
questions.explanation: The 750 hours/month are pooled across instances. Two instances 24/7 would use 1,440 hours, exceeding the free limit. You’d be charged for the extra 690 hours.

questions.question: Billing data in AWS is updated approximately every ________ hours, so alarms may be delayed.
questions.explanation: Cost and usage data is updated once daily, meaning a billing alarm might not fire until the next day.

questions.question: The AWS Free Tier offers unlimited data transfer out of AWS.
questions.explanation: False. The Free Tier includes 1 GB of data transfer out per month. Extra data transfer out incurs charges.

questions.question: If you need a response time of less than 15 minutes for critical production issues, which support plan should you choose?
questions.explanation: Enterprise offers a 15‑minute response time for business‑critical issues. Business offers 1‑hour response.

questions.question: Which of the following is a free resource for AWS community help?
questions.explanation: re:Post is a free community forum. Developer Support costs money, full Trusted Advisor requires higher plans, and TAM requires Enterprise.
